description: Real LLM benchmark tasks against more complex external GitHub projects with non-trivial parser/runtime behavior. Workspaces are cloned from fixed commits and verified through hidden behavioral contracts plus real project tests.

tasks.title: picomatch array-pattern matchers should preserve returnObject diagnostics
tasks.prompt: In the real picomatch codebase, single-pattern matchers support a second argument `returnObject=true` that returns the full match result object, but array-pattern matchers currently collapse matched results to booleans. Update array-pattern matchers so `picomatch(['*.js', '*.md'])('readme.md', true)` returns the matched pattern's result object with `isMatch: true`, `glob: '*.md'`, `input`, and `output`, while the default call without `returnObject` still returns booleans. Preserve callbacks such as `onResult` as each candidate pattern is evaluated. Add focused in-project coverage in test/api.picomatch.js with verifier-visible wording around array patterns and returnObject, including a later-pattern match such as `*.md`. Keep the change scoped to lib/picomatch.js and test/api.picomatch.js only. Do not modify package metadata, dependency files, README, parser internals, or build output. Run the verifier before finishing, using the verifier command exactly as provided.

anti_shortcut_rules: Do not modify package metadata, dependency files, README, parser internals, or build output for this task.
Implement the runtime behavior in lib/picomatch.js and add focused runtime coverage in test/api.picomatch.js.
Array-pattern matchers must accept the same `returnObject=true` second argument as single-pattern matchers.
When a later pattern matches, such as `*.md`, the returned object must identify that matched glob rather than only returning `true`.
The default array-pattern API without `returnObject` must keep returning booleans.
Preserve onResult callbacks while each candidate pattern is evaluated.
Name the new test with verifier-visible wording such as `array patterns returnObject`.
Do not claim success until the provided verifier passes.

tasks.title: yargs-parser array options should honor narg:0 without consuming values
tasks.prompt: In the real yargs-parser codebase, normal options with `narg: 0` do not consume the following argument and reject `--flag=value` with `Argument unexpected for: flag`. Array options should obey the same zero-argument contract. Update array option parsing so `parser(['--items', 'positional', '--other', 'value'], { array: ['items'], narg: { items: 0 } })` returns `items: []`, leaves `positional` in `argv._`, and still parses `other: 'value'`. Also ensure `parser.detailed(['--items=unexpected'], { array: ['items'], narg: { items: 0 } })` reports `Argument unexpected for: items`, and that aliases such as `-i` for `items` preserve the same empty-array result. Preserve existing array+narg behavior for positive counts such as `narg: { items: 1 }`. Add focused in-project coverage in test/yargs-parser.mjs with verifier-visible wording around array narg zero. Keep the change scoped to lib/yargs-parser.ts and test/yargs-parser.mjs only. Do not modify package metadata, build output, docs, or unrelated parser files. Run the verifier before finishing, using the verifier command exactly as provided.

anti_shortcut_rules: Do not modify package metadata, generated build output, docs, or unrelated parser helper files for this task.
Implement the runtime behavior in lib/yargs-parser.ts and add focused runtime coverage in test/yargs-parser.mjs.
Array options with narg:0 must not consume the following positional value.
Array options with narg:0 must reject --items=value with the same `Argument unexpected for: items` contract used by normal narg:0 options.
Alias forms such as -i for items must preserve the same empty-array result.
Positive array+narg counts such as narg:1 must keep consuming the configured number of values.
Name the new test with verifier-visible wording such as `array narg zero`.
Do not claim success until the provided verifier passes.
